To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Nash equilibria of the open-economy delegation game with representative bankers are inefficient and (2) delegation is not a cure to these inefficiencies, even if all countries independently delegate.

(i) in the Nash equilibrium, the fiscal–monetic balance depends on shock symmetry; (ii) the fiscal–monotic balance can be improved by appointing conservative bankers; (iii) the fiscal–monic balance is not necessarily improved by unilateral delegation; and (iv) delegation is not necessarily beneficial when all countries independently do so.
the delegation game is not a good model for understanding fiscal policy in the open economy.
